paper.title: LLM-Prop: predicting the properties of crystalline materials using large language models
paper.research_summary: The paper introduces LLM-Prop, a method that leverages large language models (LLMs) to predict physical and electronic properties of crystalline materials from their natural language text descriptions—bypassing traditional graph-based representations. It proposes a benchmark dataset (TextEdge), develops a fine-tuned T5 encoder architecture with specialized preprocessing (e.g., [NUM]/[ANG] tokenization, [CLS] prepending, label scaling), and demonstrates superior performance over state-of-the-art GNNs and domain-specific LLMs (e.g., MatBERT) on six crystal properties including band gap, unit cell volume, formation energy, and band gap type classification.

tasks.task_name_raw: predicting the properties of crystalline materials
tasks.objective: predicting physical and electronic properties of crystalline materials from their text descriptions
target_properties: whether the band gap is direct or indirect
output_goal: predicted numerical values for regression tasks (e.g., band gap in eV, volume in A³/cell) and class labels for classification tasks (e.g., direct/indirect band gap)

evidence.text: LLM-Prop: predicting the properties of crystalline materials using large language models

Our LLM-Prop framework (Fig. 1a) is composed of a carefully fine-tuned encoder part of small version of T5 model (Fig. 1b)31 on text descriptions of crystal structures to learn crystal representations that are used to predict the physical and electronic properties of any crystal material.

We focus on six crystal properties that include both regression and classification tasks and are diverse enough to evaluate the capabilities of any property predictor. We collect the data of band gap, formation energy per atom (FEPA), energy above hull (Ehull), crystal volume, energy per atom (EPA), and an indicator of whether the band gap is direct or indirect (Is-gap-direct).

evidence.text: In this paper, we develop and make public a benchmark dataset (TextEdge) that contains crystal text descriptions with their properties.
Finally, we release to the public the curated dataset we used as a benchmark, called TextEdge, to accelerate natural language processing (NLP) for materials science research.

We focus on six crystal properties that include both regression and classification tasks and are diverse enough to evaluate the capabilities of any property predictor. We collect the data of band gap, formation energy per atom (FEPA), energy above hull (Ehull), crystal volume, energy per atom (EPA), and an indicator of whether the band gap is direct or indirect (Is-gap-direct).

The data originally contained 145,825 crystals structure-description pairs which we randomly split into 125,825 samples for the training set, 10,000 samples for the validation set and 10,000 samples for the test set.
